\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مامور} (ma'mur)}{مامور (ma'mur)}]{\fa{مامور} (ma'mur) — an officer, an agent}

\label{lesson:FA-C319-mamur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to attack, then the Persian for a weapon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مامور}}
\textbf{\fa{مامور}} (\emph{ma'mur}) — \textquotedblleft{}an officer, an agent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دو} \fa{مامور} \fa{پلیس} \fa{جلوی} \fa{در} \fa{ایستاده} \fa{بودند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do ma'mur-e polis jelo-ye dar istâde budand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two police officers were standing at the door.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{ma'murân}. Careful print adds a hamza sign over the alef.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ma'mur} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ma'mūr} (EtymDB), the passive participle \textquotedblleft{}one who is given an order\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ma'mur}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ma'mur}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ma'mur}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to attack, then the Persian for a weapon, then say \emph{ma'mur} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گشت} (gasht)}{گشت (gasht)}]{\fa{گشت} (gasht) — a patrol}

\label{lesson:FA-C319-gasht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a weapon, then the Persian for an officer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گشت}}
\textbf{\fa{گشت}} (\emph{gasht}) — \textquotedblleft{}a patrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گشت} \fa{پلیس} \fa{هر} \fa{شب} \fa{از} \fa{کوچه} \fa{ما} \fa{رد} \fa{میشود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gasht-e polis har shab az kuche-ye mâ radd mishavad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A police patrol goes through our street every night.
\end{quote}

From \emph{gashtan} \textquotedblleft{}to go round\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Gasht zadan} is \textquotedblleft{}to stroll about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gasht} is the past stem of the native verb \emph{gashtan} \textquotedblleft{}to turn, to go round\textquotedblright{}, used as a noun. EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مظنون} (maznun)}{مظنون (maznun)}]{\fa{مظنون} (maznun) — a suspect; suspected}

\label{lesson:FA-C319-maznun}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an officer, then the Persian for a patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مظنون}}
\textbf{\fa{مظنون}} (\emph{maznun}) — \textquotedblleft{}a suspect; suspected\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{با} \fa{دو} \fa{مظنون} \fa{صحبت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis bâ do maznun sohbat kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police spoke with two suspects.
\end{quote}

As an adjective: \emph{maznun be dozdi} \textquotedblleft{}suspected of theft\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{maznun} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{maẓnūn}, \textquotedblleft{}suspected, imagined\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دستگیر} \fa{شدن} (dastgir shodan)}{دستگیر شدن (dastgir shodan)}]{\fa{دستگیر} \fa{شدن} (dastgir shodan) — to be arrested, to be caught}

\label{lesson:FA-C319-dastgir-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a patrol, then the Persian for a suspect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دستگیر} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{دستگیر} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{dastgir shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be arrested, to be caught\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دزد} \fa{دو} \fa{روز} \fa{بعد} \fa{دستگیر} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dozd do ruz ba'd dastgir shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief was arrested two days later.
\end{quote}

\emph{dast} \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{} + \emph{gir} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}: caught by the hand. Present \emph{dastgir mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dastgir} joins \emph{dast} \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Old Persian \emph{dasta-} (EtymDB), and \emph{gir-}, the present stem of \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}. \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dastgir shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dastgir shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a patrol, then the Persian for a suspect, then say \emph{dastgir shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بازداشت} \fa{کردن} (bâzdâsht kardan)}{بازداشت کردن (bâzdâsht kardan)}]{\fa{بازداشت} \fa{کردن} (bâzdâsht kardan) — to detain, to take into custody}

\label{lesson:FA-C319-bazdasht-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a suspect, then the Persian for to be arrested.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بازداشت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بازداشت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{bâzdâsht kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to detain, to take into custody\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{راننده} \fa{را} \fa{برای} \fa{چند} \fa{ساعت} \fa{بازداشت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis rânande râ barâ-ye chand sâ'at bâzdâsht kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police detained the driver for a few hours.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâsht} \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}: to hold back. Present \emph{bâzdâsht mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâzdâsht} joins \emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}back, again\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dâsht}, the past stem of \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to hold, to have\textquotedblright{}; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
